facts.statement: Meridiosaurus is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian belonging to the family Pholidosauridae.
facts.quote: Meridiosaurus is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian that is a member of the family Pholidosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus was described in 1980 based on a partial rostrum containing the premaxillae and most of the maxillae.
facts.quote: The genus was described in 1980 on the basis of a partial rostrum that included the premaxillae and most of the maxillae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Meridiosaurus have been found in the Late Jurassic Tacuarembó Formation in Tacuarembó, Uruguay.
facts.quote: Remains have been found in the Late Jurassic Tacuarembó Formation in Tacuarembó, Uruguay.

facts.statement: While some authors doubt the assignment of Meridiosaurus to Pholidosauridae, a 2011 redescription and phylogenetic analysis confirmed this classification.
facts.quote: The assignment to Pholidosauridae is considered doubtful by some authors, but a 2011 redescription and phylogenetic analysis confirmed the pholidosaurid classification of Meridiosaurus.

facts.statement: Meridiosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)
